rubrics.criterion: After the patch, the layout of the composite raw store key (the configured key prefix, the record-identity segment and the record key joined with the `||` separator) is determined by exactly one shared production implementation, and the base store driver's read, write, delete and enumeration operations all obtain the raw keys they persist or sweep through that implementation instead of rebuilding the key in their own bodies.
rubrics.rationale: The four lifecycle operations of the store driver each hold a private inline copy of the key layout in this instance; consolidating them under one owner is the central outcome the task prompt asks for.

rubrics.criterion: After the patch, the record-identity digest (salt parts joined with the `||` separator and hashed with the FIPS-safe MD5 call) is computed by exactly one shared production implementation, and both digest sites — the derivation of a source image's stored identity and the derivation of the thumbnail destination filename — obtain their digests through it.
rubrics.rationale: The identity digest is the second record-identification scheme duplicated inline in this instance; a conceptual change to it must not require edits in more than one place, and leaving either site with a private copy keeps the maintenance problem unsolved.

rubrics.criterion: After the patch, both bulk purge flows — the generic emergency clear of the store driver, and the database+cache store's purge that matches cache entries and key-value rows — derive their sweep/match terms from the shared key implementation rather than composing prefix-and-separator terms locally.
rubrics.rationale: This instance specifically placed layout knowledge into both purge flows, which only remove records whose keys they can reconstruct; a consolidation that rewires record operations but leaves the purges composing their own terms would still require scheme changes to be edited in the purge paths.

rubrics.criterion: After the patch, the enumeration path returns bare record keys by delegating the raw-key dismantle to the shared key implementation (recovering exactly the same record keys as before), rather than stripping key segments inside the scanning method itself.
rubrics.rationale: Undoing the composite raw key is one half of the raw-key layout knowledge that this instance scattered into the scan operation separately from construction; without routing it through the owner, the record-identity layout is still known by non-owning code.

rubrics.criterion: The patch leaves one or more of the previously scattered inline copies in place — for example an inline composite-key build inside any store lifecycle method (read, write, delete or enumeration), a locally composed prefix-and-separator term inside either bulk-clear flow, or an inline digest computation inside the image identity property or the thumbnail destination-filename derivation — even if a shared implementation was also added elsewhere.
rubrics.rationale: A typical incomplete repair for this case adds a central helper but only rewires the copies the solver noticed first; this instance's copies deliberately take four different syntactic shapes and live in five files, so verifying that each host was actually emptied is material to completion.

rubrics.criterion: The patch leaves behind machinery that only served the inline copies or that duplicates the new owner — for example digest-related imports (the hashing module or the stringification helper imported for local salt building) still imported by the backend and image modules that no longer compute digests inline, or more than one parallel helper left in the tree doing the raw-key or digest job with unused duplicates.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state added local hashing imports to the backend and image modules and removed the former central helpers; a complete cleanup in this instance removes support imports the consolidation made dead and does not leave duplicated or caller-less scheme helpers.

rubrics.criterion: The patch changes the byte content of any identifier the schemes produce — a composite raw key, an identity-scoped scan or purge term, a digest, or a generated thumbnail filename — for example by reordering salt parts, stringifying parts differently, using a different separator or number of separator segments, or matching purge terms against a differently scoped prefix.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's behavioral bar is byte-identical identifiers: existing deployments hold files, cache entries and store rows under the current format, and the repository's tests assert exact generated thumbnail filenames, so any drift is a functional regression of the refactoring.

rubrics.criterion: After the patch, a bulk purge sweeps a different key set than before — for example matching only one record-identity segment because the purge term was rebuilt around a specific identity instead of all raw keys of the installation, or conversely missing the prefix-plus-separator boundary — so an emergency clear would leave cache entries or database rows behind or destroy keys it must not touch.
rubrics.rationale: Both purge flows in this instance must keep sweeping every raw key of the installation while the record operations keep writing keys through the new owner; reconnecting the purges to a rebuilt term is exactly where a plausible subtle regression of this case appears.

rubrics.criterion: The new scheme owners capture part of the key layout at import time — for example module-level constants evaluated from Django settings before settings are finalized, instead of reading the configured key prefix inside the owning functions at call time.
rubrics.rationale: The key prefix knob exists precisely to isolate installations in shared stores; this case's compatibility boundary requires the schemes to continue following the configured settings at call time, and freezing them at import time breaks deployments that override the knob.
